summary.text: A previously healthy 6-year-old female was admitted with seven days of fever, cough and fatigue and a positive PCR test for COVID-19 infection. Relatives had been infected before she became symptomatic. She had sore throat, nausea and abdominal pain but no diarrhea. On admission she was febrile and tachypneic, with oxygen saturation 86% on room air, 92% with supplemental oxygen at 5 L/min. No jaundice, hepatomegaly or splenomegaly was present.

Chest CT showed scattered nodular opacities and right middle lobe consolidation, and abdominal sonogram was normal. Admission ALT and AST were reported as 286 and 217 U/L, while Table 1 labels the first-day values the other way round. Serial laboratory results included ferritin, CRP, ESR, white cell and platelet counts, D-dimer, LDH, CPK, pro-BNP, SGOT and SGPT. Pneumonia with elevated liver enzymes was diagnosed.

She received remdesivir 5 mg/kg on the first day and 2.5 mg/kg from the second to the fifth day of treatment, with dexamethasone started simultaneously. Fever subsided after 48 hours but returned on the sixth hospital day, oxygen demand did not fall, meropenem was added for probable bacterial superinfection, and repeat chest CT showed partial resolution of RML consolidation.

Oxygen requirement fell to 2-3 L/min on day 8 of treatment and supplemental oxygen was stopped on day 10 of hospitalization. ALT and AST decreased during remdesivir therapy, approaching normal values at discharge. She was discharged after 14 days of hospitalization, and one- and two-week follow-up visits revealed no complications.
